- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1.5–2x recent high to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.1) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.0 to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — adjust downward bias by 0.5–1.0 in first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum — increase forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0 to mid-period values.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.3–0.7 to align with historical volatility.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds model by > 2.0 in any 5-day window, apply “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 0.2–0.5 per day for next 3–5 days.
